title: Identity Champion — Advanced Algebraic Identities
learningGoals: Expand cube identities (a+b)³ and (a-b)³ with confidence
Factorise sum and difference of cubes using standard identities
Apply cube identities to compute numeric expressions mentally
coreIdeas: Binomial cube coefficients follow Pascal's triangle row 1,3,3,1
Sum/difference of cubes always factor into a linear × quadratic term
Substituting numbers into identities enables rapid mental arithmetic

onboarding.welcomeMessage: Welcome, Identity Champion! Today you master cube identities that unlock lightning-fast mental math.

duolingoLessonArc.mission: Master cube expansions and cube factorisations — handle (a+b)³, (a-b)³, a³+b³, and a³-b³ fluently.
microLessonPattern: Coach introduces concept with board demo

reviewLoop.action: Show worked example, then retry with new numbers

sessionFlow.coachHook: Before we climb to cubes, let's polish our squares!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Write (a+b)²=a²+2ab+b² and (a-b)²=a²-2ab+b² side by side. Highlight sign difference.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud: 'a plus b squared equals a squared plus 2ab plus b squared.'
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: Both expansions correct with correct signs.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Brilliant! You remembered both sign patterns.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Check the middle term sign — plus for (a+b)², minus for (a-b)².
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Revisit the sign rule: (a-b)² has -2ab in the middle.

exercises.hint: Set a=x and b=5, then substitute.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Squares had 3 terms. Cubes have 4! Meet Pascal's triangle row: 1, 3, 3, 1.
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Write (a+b)³ = a³+3a²b+3ab²+b³. Circle coefficients 1,3,3,1. Show a=x,b=2 example.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud the full expansion: 'a cubed plus 3 a-squared b plus 3 a b-squared plus b cubed.'
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: List the four terms one by one: a³, then 3a²b, then 3ab², then b³.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Memorise the pattern: powers of a go 3,2,1,0 and powers of b go 0,1,2,3.

exercises.hint: a=x, b=2. Compute each term: x³, 3x²·2, 3x·4, 8.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Subtract b instead of adding? Two terms go negative. Spot the pattern!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Write (a-b)³ = a³-3a²b+3ab²-b³. Highlight alternating signs. Compare with (a+b)³.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud: 'a cubed MINUS 3 a-squared b PLUS 3 ab-squared MINUS b cubed.'
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: Correct signs on all four terms.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: The sign pattern is locked in!
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Remember: (a-b)³ has signs +,-,+,- on terms 1-4 if you factor out a-b direction.

exercises.hint: a=x, b=3. Check signs carefully: -, then +, then -.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Two perfect cubes added together? One formula breaks them apart every time.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud: 'a cubed plus b cubed equals a plus b, times a squared minus ab plus b squared.'
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: Correctly identifies a=x, b=2 and writes (x+2)(x²-2x+4).
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Cube cracker! You split the sum perfectly.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: In the quadratic factor, the middle term is -ab (negative). Check your sign.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: The quadratic a²-ab+b² never factors further over integers.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Four options, one truth. Use your identity knowledge to eliminate wrong answers.
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Show two MCQ examples on board, crossing out wrong options with reasoning.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read each option carefully before selecting.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Answer the MCQ questions — no shortcuts!

sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Substitute a small value like a=1,b=1 to check which option matches.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Plug in numbers to verify: if a=1,b=1, (a+b)³=8, not 4 or 6.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Step by Step — Build the Cube
sessionFlow.coachHook: No shortcuts here — fill each step and watch the expansion build itself.
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Show the 4-step scaffold: term1=a³, term2=3a²b, term3=3ab², term4=b³.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read each step label aloud as you fill it in.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Full marks on every step — you built the cube!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Go back to the step that is wrong. Recalculate just that term.

exercises.questionText: Expand (2x+3)³ step by step. Fill each term.

sessionFlow.coachHook: 101 is just 100+1. Use the identity and mental math does the rest!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Write 101=(100+1). Apply (a+b)³ with a=100,b=1. Show each term: 1000000+30000+300+1.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud: '100 cubed is 1 million. 3 times 100 squared is 30 thousand.'
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Compute 102³ mentally using the same method.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Choose a=100 as a round base to keep arithmetic easy.

exercises.questionText: Compute 101³ mentally. Write 101 = 100+1 and apply the cube identity.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Last identity: a³-b³. The sign in the quadratic flips. Master this and you own all four cube rules!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Write a³-b³=(a-b)(a²+ab+b²). Compare with sum of cubes — only (a-b) and +ab differ. Verify with a=3,b=2: 27-8=19=(1)(9+6+4)=19 ✓
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud: 'a cubed MINUS b cubed equals a MINUS b, times a squared PLUS ab plus b squared.'
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: All four cube identities mastered — Identity Champion unlocked!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Compare with sum of cubes: here the linear factor is (a-b) and the middle sign in the quadratic is +ab.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Memory trick — the quadratic always has +ab for difference, -ab for sum.

exercises.hint: 27=3³. Set a=x, b=3. The quadratic factor is a²+ab+b².
